housemouse: A house mouse, a SMALL slender rodent about the length of a thumb in the body, with a POINTED NARROW SNOUT, LARGE THIN ROUNDED EARS STANDING WELL CLEAR OF THE FUR, prominent black bead eyes and long fine whiskers. Its tail is THIN, NEARLY HAIRLESS, FINELY RINGED AND AS LONG AS ITS HEAD AND BODY TOGETHER. Soft dusty grey-brown fur, paler beneath.
brownrat: A brown rat, a LARGE heavy rodent much bigger than a mouse, with a BLUNT THICK SNOUT, SMALL THICK ROUNDED EARS set close to the head, small dark eyes and a heavy-shouldered body. Its tail is THICK AT THE BASE, COARSELY SCALED, SPARSELY HAIRED AND SHORTER THAN ITS HEAD AND BODY. Coarse shaggy grizzled brown fur, greyish beneath, with large pink feet.
fieldvole: A field vole, a SMALL round-bodied rodent with a BLUNT ROUNDED BLUNT-NOSED FACE quite unlike a mouse's pointed one, SMALL EARS ALMOST BURIED IN ITS FUR AND BARELY VISIBLE, and tiny black eyes. Its tail is SHORT AND FURRED, ONLY ABOUT A THIRD THE LENGTH OF ITS BODY. Its coat is long, shaggy and greyish-brown, giving it a plump untidy outline.
commontoad: A common toad squatting, a squat heavy-bodied amphibian with DRY ROUGH WARTY SKIN in dull olive, brown and grey, a broad blunt head, and SHORT STURDY LEGS held tucked so it sits low and hunched. Its eyes are the point: LARGE, COPPER-ORANGE, WITH A HORIZONTAL SLOT-SHAPED PUPIL LYING FLAT ACROSS THEM. A large raised oval gland sits behind each eye.
grasssnake: A grass snake, a slim olive-green snake with a slender body and keeled scales, lying in a loose open curve, with round pupils in a large eye and a slightly rounded snout. The marking that identifies it is at the neck: a BOLD COLLAR OF BRIGHT YELLOW OR CREAM CROSSED BY A BLACK CRESCENT just behind the head. Small black bars run along its flanks.
eurasianmagpie: A Eurasian magpie standing, a large boldly PIED crow with a CLEAN WHITE BELLY AND WHITE PATCHES ON THE FOLDED WING, everything else black. The black is not flat: it carries a strong IRIDESCENT GLOSS OF BOTTLE-GREEN AND VIOLET-BLUE across the wing and tail. Its TAIL IS VERY LONG AND WEDGE-SHAPED, longer than the whole rest of the bird. Stout black bill.
eurasianskylark: A Eurasian skylark, a plump ground-dwelling songbird in streaky sandy brown and cream, heavily marked with dark streaks over the back and across the upper breast, with a pale belly and a WHITE OUTER EDGE TO THE TAIL. Its crown carries a SHORT BLUNT ERECTILE CREST raised into a small rounded peak. Slim pale bill, long straight hind claw.
europeanmole: A European mole, a small CYLINDRICAL sausage-shaped animal with DENSE VELVETY BLACK-GREY FUR, a pointed pink fleshy snout, and no visible ears or eyes in the fur. Its front paws are the point: ENORMOUS, BROAD, PINK AND SPADE-SHAPED, far out of proportion to the body, TURNED PERMANENTLY OUTWARD AND BACKWARD like a pair of oars, tipped with heavy pale claws.
europeanbadger: A European badger standing in side view, a heavy low-slung animal with a broad body, short powerful legs and coarse grizzled silver-grey fur. Its head is the point: SMALL, WHITE, AND CROSSED BY TWO BOLD BLACK STRIPES RUNNING FROM THE MUZZLE BACK THROUGH EACH EYE TO THE EAR, so the face reads as three white bands. Small rounded white-edged ears, long pale claws.
plainspocketgopher: A plains pocket gopher, a stout cylindrical burrowing rodent with a large flat head, tiny eyes and ears, and LARGE PALE CHISEL-SHAPED FRONT INCISORS PERMANENTLY EXPOSED OUTSIDE THE CLOSED LIPS. Its forepaws carry LONG HEAVY CURVED DIGGING CLAWS, and a FUR-LINED POUCH OPENS ON THE OUTSIDE OF EACH CHEEK, bulging when full. Short sparsely haired tail, brown fur.
